adapt: Unfamiliar project? Reads the code and local rules so the next task starts with the facts.
architect: Making a big technical choice? Compares tradeoffs and records decisions that change system boundaries.
audit: Reviewing a plan or change? Flags defects and risks with evidence and next steps.
author: Writing docs or filing issues? Turns scattered facts into clear copy or actionable tickets.
brief: Pausing or handing off? Captures the next step, what’s approved, and what to recheck.
clean: Cleaning up or committing? Checks what can go and protects unrelated work.
code: Implementing in a known stack? Brings in patterns and pitfalls for the language and version in use.
debug: Something broke? Traces the failure to its cause and checks the smallest fix.
deploy: Rolling out a change or handling an incident? Checks live health and guides rollout or recovery.
design: Creating or revising visuals? Sets a direction and checks the result as users see it.
equip: Choosing a tool or format? Compares fit and switching cost before changing course.
execute: Default for any task. Keeps the work direct and reports only what matters.
market: Positioning an offer or planning a campaign? Uses audience evidence to shape the message and next action.
migrate: Changing stored data or schemas? Defines what to preserve and how to recover.
plan: Coordinating complex work? Turns the agreed outcome into steps, checks, and handoffs.
preflight: Unsure the environment can run the task? Finds missing tools or incompatible setup.
refactor: Simplifying existing code? Improves the structure and checks that behavior stays the same.
search: Need outside evidence? Investigates beyond the project and shows what the sources support.
ship: Deciding what to build or launch? Weighs user evidence, priorities, and how to measure success.
test: Need to verify a result? Runs focused checks and reports what passed and what’s unverified.
